findings.evidence: Line 149: `((trialLaw μ g).restrict (acceptSet f g c)).map Prod.fst`; line 170 `theorem trialLaw_acceptSet`; upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Prod.lean:257 `lemma map_fst_prod : Measure.map Prod.fst (μ.prod ν) = …`.
findings.issue: `map_fst_restrict_acceptSet` omits the measure being restricted, so the name reads as a statement about restricting an arbitrary measure to the accept set; the companion lemma about the same object names it (`trialLaw_acceptSet`, line 170), as do both generic lemmas in this PR (`map_fst_restrict_prod`, `…_prod_uniformMeasure`).

summary: Three names do not match their statements: a lemma specialised to `uniformMeasure 0 1` is named as if it held for every interval, `acceptedLaw_eq`/`acceptedLaw_ne_…` read as an eq/ne pair despite different right-hand sides, and the flagship lemma omits the `trialLaw` its companion names. I do not re-raise the `setOf_le` ordering or the single `of_` clause in the silent-bias name; both are as this thread's earlier round asked.
